decisions.statement: A construction is found in the tree rather than in the words.
A word read as a noun with neither a clause nor an object names no action of that word.
A word read as a noun that has an object of its own is read as an action.
A word whose object comes before it has an object.
A word taking a particle is left alone.
A word bound to something by `to` and with no object is left alone.
Which spellings are one word is the caller's to say.
A word in the passive that puts a thing somewhere is the same construction.
A `to` phrase binds the word rather than placing a thing.
A word whose only subject is the relativizer is left alone.
A word whose object is the relativizer and that has no subject of its own is left alone.
A bare adverb after a word is a particle whatever the parser calls it.
A word a person or an unknown is the holder of is left alone.
A word a preposition comes before names an act.
A word whose object before it is a pronoun is left alone.
A word a past participle comes right after is left alone.
A past participle is a word read as a verb and spelled with a trailing `ed` or `en`.
A particle right after a word is that word's particle whatever the parser calls it.
A particle the parser hung on a word's object is that word's particle.
A particle right after a word's object is that word's particle unless the particle marks a phrase.
A `to` phrase the parser hung on a word's object binds that word.
A directed preposition binds a word as `to` does.
A word a form of `have` comes right after is left alone.
A word the parser gave a form of `have` for an auxiliary is left alone.
A word set against another word by `rather than` is left alone.
A word a preposition the parser hung on as an adverb strands is left alone.
A word whose object is a self is left alone.
A word whose object a preposition hangs off is left alone.
A directed preposition after a word's object sends that object on.
A participle an adverb comes before is left alone.
A participle beside another clause on the same word is left alone.
A participle either side of a joining is left alone.
A participle read as a clause of its own names an act.
A word with no object that places a thing somewhere is left alone.
A word read as a noun that heads a relative clause is read as an action.
A thing right before a word with no subject of its own is that word's subject.
A word whose object is a question is left alone.
A word the parser gave two objects a name could fill is left alone.
A word whose object is read as neither a thing nor a pronoun is left alone.
A fronted word joined to another word is left alone.
A word spelled with a trailing `ing` is a participle whatever it hangs on.
A participle under a form of `be` names an act.
A participle with no word before it names an act.
A participle read as a clause's own subject names an act.

definition: where a construction is in a sentence, read off that sentence's tree
